title: How Doctors die. It’s not like the rest of us (2016)
summary: A reflective essay exploring how medical professionals approach end-of-life care differently from the general public, revealing that doctors tend to choose comfort over aggressive treatment when facing terminal illness. The article highlights the disconnect between what patients and families often demand in final medical interventions versus what physicians choose for themselves.
problem_solved: Addresses the disconnect between patient expectations and medical reality at the end of life.
why_valuable: Provides rare insider perspective on end-of-life decisions, helping readers understand why informed medical professionals often choose palliative care over aggressive interventions.
